### problem_chain

Root: the customer asks for an on-demand payout of what is available today (persona: "you would like to take an on-demand payout today of the money that is available … sent to the bank account you have on file"); owner=user (`request_on_demand_payout_667d53e6`), handed over by the agent. The persona raises nothing else; it names no prerequisite (it only says, conditionally, that if the agent explains something must be booked first it is fine — a passive reaction, not a hint toward any specific problem).

Walking the root's rule, its prerequisite sentences and the opening world:

| edge | sentence (root rule) | state at frozen_time (DB evidence) | resolving rule / write | kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 | "An on-demand payout is fixed only after the scheduled payout due on the same payout day stands on the payments ledger." | Plan `Payments Daily Plus` (`payout_accounts.40e996b8….variant_name`), `payout_schedule_rule: every_business_day`; 2026-10-15 is a business day; account `active`; bank hold (3 days from `bank_changed_date` 2026-09-25) ended 2026-09-28; payable 45425.05 − 1700.00 = 43725.05 ≥ `min_payout_amount` 1.0 ⇒ a scheduled payout is due today. Ledger has no `payout_disbursement` with `payout_method=scheduled` dated 2026-10-15 (last scheduled: `6f83f7bb…` 2026-10-02). **Unmet.** | payout_ext_scheduled_payout_limit -> `send_scheduled_payout_7857f918` (agent) | value_input (balance -> payable_now) |
| E2 | "An on-demand payout is not worked out until every chargeback case whose dispute is recorded as won carries its returned-debit entry on the payments ledger." | `payout_chargeback_disputes.a8eb203c…` case CB-20260908-2264 `won`; ledger has no `payout_chargeback_reversal` on that case. **Unmet.** | payout_ext_won_chargeback_debit_return -> `return_won_chargeback_debit_b5e77014` (agent) | value_input (balance -> payable_now; and returned_debits_6m) |
| E3 | "Before an on-demand payout amount is worked out, every instant payout already sent that day must carry its instant payout fee entry on the payments ledger." | `payout_events.48003b2d…` instant payout IP-20261015-525, 6400.00, dated 2026-10-15; no `payout_instant_fee` naming IP-20261015-525. **Unmet.** | payout_ext_instant_fee_posting -> `post_instant_payout_fee_64da22a6` (agent) | value_input (balance -> payable_now) |

The three depended-on policies have `prerequisite: []`; their own rules carry no prerequisite sentence, so the tree stops. Derived tree: root on_demand with three children, n = 3, three `value_input` edges (floor max(n−1,1) = 2), one owner=user write (the root), no cycle. Topological order: {scheduled payout, instant fee, debit return} in any order, then on-demand payout.

Parallel edges: the three children share the balance. Scheduled amount = min(payable, 33,000.00); the lowest payable any order can present is 43725.05 − 54.72 = 43670.33 > 33,000.00, so the scheduled amount is 33,000.00 in all six orders; the instant fee and the debit return read no balance. All six orders give the same three amounts and the same terminal state. No two-solution order.

Load-bearing (skip one child write, replay the rest, recompute the on-demand payout): skip scheduled -> 37,424.96; skip instant fee -> 6,126.95; skip debit return -> 4,411.81; full tree -> 6,074.96. Every edge bears weight.

Other DB facts checked: the other dispute (CB-20260804-1187) is `lost` — no debit return due; the fee-return rule gives 0 for CB-20260908-2264 (Daily Plus `chargeback_fee_refunded_on_win: false`, evidence refund_already_issued ⇒ evidence share 0) — no fee-return write and it is not in this tree; the only reserve still held (order afec5592, 1700.00, shipped, promised 2026-10-18 ⇒ release 2026-10-25) is not due; the three reserves due 2026-10-15 are already released (rows a3ab240a…, cae62ecd…, 2bc1d95e…). ## findings

- **T0-1 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED.** Symptom: the instant-fee and on-demand computations each declare one `method` factor whose tiers only change a window length. Root cause: charter-global F-1 (`_difficulty.md` § findings). Evidence: `pricing_volume_window` = (12/w)·Σ_w sale credits with w = 6 taken here (530,000.00), baseline w = 12 (430,000.00); `reserve_base_window` = (1/w)·Σ_w with w = 3 taken (50,000.00), baseline w = 12 (35,833.33). Demonstrated consequence: substituting w is substituting a number into one formula — the 69.12 and 6,606.21 sub values come from the same algorithm with a different w; with the label struck, the instant fee (54.72) and the on-demand payout (6,074.96) carry 0 `method` factors against a floor of 1. Affected: `payout.extended.yaml` factors of payout_ext_instant_fee_posting and payout_ext_on_demand_payout; computations steps 15 and 17. Previous revision: none (first audit).
- **T0-2 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED.** Symptom: the debit-return computation in this tree carries an unreal ladder tier. Root cause: charter-global F-2. Evidence: rule sentence on item_as_described_evidence; base `payout_chargebacks` sentence "the seller never bears both the refund and the chargeback for the same order amount". Demonstrated consequence: on this task's order 0518e2c2 (sale credit 2,860.00, seller-funded refund 1,150.00, chargeback 2,860.00), had the same dispute been won on item_as_described evidence, the tier returns 2,860.00 − 1,150.00 − 3.00 = 1,707.00, leaving the seller at 2,860.00 − 1,150.00 − 2,860.00 − 15.00 + 1,707.00 = −1,458.00 on an order whose dispute it won — the refunded 1,150.00 borne twice. Scored value 1,147.00 is not moved (refund_already_issued tier taken). Affected: factor `evidence_return_basis` of payout_ext_won_chargeback_debit_return; computation step 13. Previous revision: none.
- **T0-3 — SOURCE-TASK RED.** Symptom: the world contradicts the inherited base instant-payout rules and the rationale asserts it does not. Root cause: seed rows `payout_events.d7f0fd2d…` (instant 4,000.00 on 2026-08-27 from a payable amount of 0.00, balance driven to −1,185.00) and `payout_events.48003b2d…` (instant 6,400.00 on 2026-10-15 above the 5,000.00 daily limit); `design_rationale` "[World] … simulated day by day under the base rules". Evidence: running-sum recomputation above; base `payout_instant_terms` and `payout_disbursement_schedule` sentences quoted above. Demonstrated consequence: the scored instant fee's `frequency_discount` tier (2 instant payouts in three months ⇒ 0.0005) rests on the 2026-08-27 row the charter says cannot exist; without that row the three-month count is 1 ⇒ discount 0 ⇒ fee 57.60 instead of 54.72, and (holding the seeded opening balance) the on-demand payout 6,072.23 instead of 6,074.96 (payable 11,814.45, compliance 590.72).
